newsitem.title: USA: Dry Kansas wheat areas may receive rain by Friday.
newsitem.headline: Dry Kansas wheat areas may receive rain by Friday.

text.p: Rain was forecast for dry northwest Kansas late Thursday and Friday, but after that the area turns dry again, meteorologists said.

"We are looking at something on the order of a quarter to three-quarters of an inch (rain) for northeast Colorado, northwest Kansas and southwest Nebraska," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.

Extremely dry conditions in western and northwest Kansas slowed development of hard red winter wheat and delayed sorghum planting, grain dealers said. However, recent cool weather there has kept the wheat's moisture needs down.
Burgio said Goodland, in northwest Kansas, has received 0.37 inch of rain so far this month, which is 16 percent of the normal 2.25 inches received by this date.
"The next 48 hours are the best chance they have (for rain)," said Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist. "I don't see it being a widespread rain, but I do see rain."
Gesser expects 0.10 to 0.75 inch amounts with 20 to 30 percent coverage Thursday and 40 to 50 percent on Friday.
The showers should then move east into eastern Kansas and into the Midwest.
Western Kansas temperatures will warm to the high 70s to low 80s degrees Fahrenheit Friday and Saturday before cooling to the low to mid-70s for much of next week, he said.
